title: Class Model Design: OOP Interview Must-Know

scenes.line1: How do you design a class model?
scenes.say: When you get a system design question, how do you turn real-world requirements into classes? What matters most in your approach?

scenes.label: Entities
scenes.sub: Identify main objects, like Books or Spaces.
scenes.say: First, identify the main entities in your domain, like Books in a library or Spaces in a parking lot.
Next, map out how these entities relate. For example, a ParkingLot has many Spaces, and a Library has many Books. Members borrow Loans.
When refining your model, prefer composition over inheritance. Composition makes your code flexible and easy to change, while inheritance can be rigid.

scenes.question: What’s a common mistake in class design?
scenes.right: Each class should have one clear responsibility.
scenes.say: A common trap is giving a class too many jobs. Remember, each class should have just one clear responsibility.
